classification.difficultyReason: Recover both square side lengths from their areas, recognise the unshaded region as one triangle spanning their combined width, and subtract its area from the total to obtain the shaded region.

content.prompt: What is the area of the shaded section?

spec.description: A horizontal pair shows the given square areas on the left and the repeated joined-square shape with its requested shaded region on the right, connected by a right-pointing arrow.
spec.mathematics: The larger and smaller squares have areas 64 cm² and 16 cm², with aligned bottom edges. The right-hand diagonal joins the larger square's top-left corner to the smaller square's bottom-right corner. Shading occupies the part of the joined shape above that diagonal. The internal square boundary remains visible.
spec.answerVisibility: Area givens appear only beneath the left figure. The right figure shows the target region without its calculated area.

answer.worked:
Using $A=l^2$, find the square side lengths.
$$\begin{align*}l_1^2&=64\\l_1&=8\text{ cm}\\l_2^2&=16\\l_2&=4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
The unshaded triangle spans the whole bottom edge, so its base is $8+4=12\text{ cm}$ and its perpendicular height is $8\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{unshaded}}&=\frac{bh}{2}\\A_{\text{unshaded}}&=\frac{12\times8}{2}\\A_{\text{unshaded}}&=48\text{ cm}^{2}\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=64+16-48\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=32\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$$
